newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION - Baabaas unhappy with scrumming-Brooke.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Baabaas unhappy with scrumming-Brooke.

text.p: LONDON, Nov 26 - The New Zealand Barbarians may have dominated their opposition to the point of running in 14 tries on Sunday, but lock Robin Brooke said the tight forwards were less than happy with their own scrummaging in the rugby tour opener.
The tourists thrashed a hapless North of England side 86-0 in atrocious conditions at Huddersfield, scoring at better than a point a minute on Sunday.
It was their only warm-up match to this weekend's international against England, and was not the hard match they were seeking.
John Hart's side may not be a full All Blacks unit, but they are taking the England match as seriously as any test.
And Brooke's assertion that the scrum performed poorly against the North of England is proof that they are still seeking the same high standards demanded by the All Blacks.
"We were pretty disappointed with the scrum," Brooke told NZPA.
"They pushed us back a couple of times, which should never have happened.
"It was a lack of concentration more than anything. As the game disintegrated a bit I think the guys' minds were out in the backs wanting to run the ball."
A performance like that against the powerful England side would have disastrous effects, although it is unlikely to happen.
England showed against Italy that they have, as ever, a forward pack to be reckoned with, and that usually brings out the best in the New Zealand unit.
Against Italy, England introduced new lock Simon Shaw, a 2m-plus 127kg giant from Bristol, and paired him with the experienced Martin Johnson.
At the front they have a developing trio of loose head Jason Leonard, hooker Mark Regan and Graham Rountree, which dominated their Italian opponents in Saturday's test.
Aside from loose head Mark Allen, the New Zealand front five will be the same as the one which played through all 10 All Black tests this year almost unchanged.
Brooke said the scrum will be working on a machine this week, but the forwards were familiar enough with each other to be able to cope.
"England have a huge pack, it's probably the biggest in the world," he added.
"They pushed Italy around at will, and though it's pretty hard to gauge against Italy, they were in control of the game everywhere.
"We're looking at it as a real challenge. We've played against them in the past, and they have always been tough."
For Brooke, 29 and a 37-test veteran, it is 1-1 against England after losing at Twickenham in 1993 then winning the World Cup semifinal last year.
The memories of Twickenham in 1993 are providing some of the motivation for Saturday, but Brooke said the emphasis will be on enjoyment.
"It's the last hit-out of the year for us so we will be going out to enjoy it," he said.
"Obviously we will be trying to win it too, there's a fair bit of interest from back home so we'll be doing our best."
Today, the injury-free tourists had an aerobic training session followed by the tour's golf challenge on a cold but sunny autumn day.

Hart will name his side tomorrow, with one of the few question marks over who will start in the No 10 jersey. Carlos Spencer and Andrew Mehrtens are in contention, and both will see action, although Spencer's performance against the North probably gives him the inside running.

Michael Jones will return on the blindside flank, with Dylan Mika dropping into the reserves, while on the right wing Hart may be tempted to start with Fijian Joeli Vidiri after his second-half hat-trick against the North.

Probable team: Christian Cullen, Joeli Vidiri, Alama Ieremia, Jonah Lomu, Lee Stensness, Carlos Spencer, Justin Marshall, Taine Randell, Andrew Blowers, Ian Jones, Robin Brooke, Michael Jones, Olo Brown, Sean Fitzpatrick (c), Mark Allen.
